name: Bull Shoals Lake
unique: A clear reservoir on the White River with 1,000 miles of shoreline, drowned trees and some of the best scuba diving in the mid south.
buzz: Divers come for the sunken town sites and fishermen for the bass; the lake is deep and cold and the wind comes up in the afternoon.

name: Norfork Lake
unique: A Ozark reservoir with 550 miles of shoreline, clear water and a trout fishery below the dam, ringed by forest.
buzz: The lake is quieter than Bull Shoals and the trout water below the dam is famous; the town of Mountain Home is the base.

name: Lake Chicot State Park
unique: The largest natural lake in the state, an oxbow of the Mississippi, with cypress trees, a campground and a boardwalk through a swamp.
buzz: The cypress and the birding are the reasons to camp and the lake is warm and shallow; the mosquitoes are serious in summer.

name: Murphy Arts District
unique: A former oil boom town's downtown turned arts district, with a restored 1920s theater, a speakeasy and a sculpture garden.
buzz: The restoration is the story and the shows book names bigger than the town; locals say it changed downtown.

name: Queen Wilhelmina State Park
unique: A lodge and overlook on the second highest peak in the state, at the Arkansas end of the Talimena Scenic Drive, with views into two states.
buzz: Motorcyclists ride the drive for the curves and the lodge is the stop; the fall color is the season and the ridge is often in cloud.

name: Greers Ferry Lake
unique: A clear lake in the foothills with sandy islands, a swim beach and the Little Red River trout water below the dam.
buzz: The islands and the clear water are the summer draw; the lake is busy on holidays and the trout fishing below the dam is year round.

name: Delta Rivers Nature Center
unique: A nature center on the Arkansas River with a swamp boardwalk, live alligators and a aquarium of river fish, free to the public.
buzz: The alligators and the boardwalk are the family stops and the center is free; it is a good break on the drive through the Delta.

name: Lake Ouachita State Park
unique: One of the cleanest lakes in the country, with 200 islands and a state park on a peninsula, near the quartz mines of the Ouachitas.
buzz: The water clarity is the reason people drive and the islands are the camping; the lake is big and the coves are quiet.

name: Buffalo National River: Tyler Bend
unique: A visitor center and campground on the Buffalo National River, the first national river in the country, with bluffs, gravel bars and floating.
buzz: The river float is the reason to come and Tyler Bend is the easy access; the water is clear and the crowds are at the outfitters.

name: Arkansas State University Museum
unique: A university museum with a mastodon skeleton, a pioneer village and a collection of Arkansas pottery, free on the Jonesboro campus.
buzz: The mastodon and the village are good with children and it is free; the pottery collection is the local surprise.

name: Square Books
unique: A bookstore on the Oxford square with a balcony over the courthouse, three floors of books and a writer's room upstairs.
buzz: Writers treat it as a pilgrimage and the readings are the local event; the balcony is the place to sit with a coffee.

name: Dockery Farms
unique: The cotton plantation where Charley Patton and Howlin' Wolf worked, called the birthplace of the blues, with the gin and the commissary still standing.
buzz: Blues pilgrims come from other countries and the site is quiet and unmarked; the fields and the old buildings are the whole visit.

name: Corinth Civil War Interpretive Center
unique: A center on the 1862 battle and the occupation of Corinth, with a water sculpture that traces the war and the earthworks outside.
buzz: The sculpture and the ranger talks are the reasons to stop; the town also has the old depot and the Contraband Camp site.

name: Tunica RiverPark
unique: A river museum and boardwalk on the Mississippi with aquariums of river fish, a replica of a 19th century riverboat and a nature trail.
buzz: The riverboat and the boardwalk are the family stops and the river is right there; the casinos across the road are the other Tunica.

name: Choctaw Indian Fair
unique: A Choctaw fair with stickball games, tribal dances, crafts and a world championship stickball tournament, on the reservation in central Mississippi.
buzz: The stickball is the reason to come and it is fast and physical; the fair is one of the oldest Native American gatherings in the country.

name: Museum of the Mississippi Delta
unique: A museum of the Delta's cotton economy, with farm equipment, a sharecropper cabin and the story of the Chinese and Italian immigrants who worked the fields.
buzz: The local history is specific and honest and the volunteers know the families; it is small and cheap.

name: Bay St. Louis Old Town
unique: A Gulf coast town of restored cottages and live oaks on the bay, with a beach, a small arts district and a rebuilt main street after Katrina.
buzz: The town is quieter than the casinos and the beach is free; the old town walk and the seafood are the reasons to stop.

name: Topeka Zoo
unique: A zoo in Gage Park with a rainforest building, tigers and a carousel, small enough to finish in a morning.
buzz: Parents like the size and the shade and the rainforest is the indoor stop; it is cheap and the park around it has a train.

name: Botanica
unique: Seventeen acres of themed gardens with a children's garden, a butterfly house and a carousel, beside the Arkansas River.
buzz: The children's garden and the butterfly house are the family stops and the Christmas lights are the winter tradition; the gardens peak in late spring.

name: Lanikai Pillbox Trail
unique: A short steep climb to two World War II concrete observation posts above Lanikai beach, with a view of the Mokulua islands and the windward coast.
buzz: Sunrise from the pillboxes is the photograph everyone wants and the trail is short but steep and rooty; parking is in a residential neighborhood.
